rationale: CRISPR-StAR (CRISPR-StAR: stochastic activation by recombination) temporal-control in vivo screen of a ~30,000-sgRNA library in A549 lung xenografts (Fenoglio et al., Cell Rep Methods 2026). The deposited file is UMI/clone-resolved long format (633 MB) with active_count and inactive_count per guide-UMI-tumor: Cre recombination produces, with equal frequency, an ACTIVE sgRNA (gene knockout) and an INACTIVE sgRNA (matched internal clonal control) in the same tumor; the knockout phenotype is the active/inactive ratio. UMI counts were aggregated per guide, summing active and inactive counts across all tumors, separately for the two biological replicate cohorts (invivo_screen = 118 mice, invivo_validation = 49 mice). BARCS models bulk sgRNA abundance, so the faithful mapping is active vs inactive as the KO effect, with cohort as a paired batch term: essential-gene guides should deplete in the active state. The 500 NTC single-guide controls calibrate. IMPORTANT: the paper states that bulk-abundance tools (MAGeCK/BAGEL/JACKS) are not suited to this clone-resolved data and built a dedicated per-clone Bayesian pipeline (CSTAR-UMIBB) using matched active/inactive controls WITHIN each clone; BARCS's bulk active-vs-inactive aggregation is the 'traditional proxy' the paper shows is weaker (their Fig 2F, r=0.43 without internal normalization vs r=0.8 with per-clone weighting), so this reanalysis tests essential-gene recovery at the bulk level, not the paper's per-clone wtheta / Delta scores.
